scope: Theorem 2.1 (Algebraic lifting) of the manuscript “A Counterexample to Kurosh’s Division-Ring Problem” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-Kuroshs-Division-Ring-Problem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 201 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9195b0a83fc63370), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let k be a countable field of characteristic zero containing every root of unity, and let A be a finite-dimensional central division algebra over k. Suppose X ∈ A⟨⟨z1, z2⟩⟩u satisfies: (i) X0 generates A as a k-algebra; (ii) X1, X2 have linearly independent classes in Au/JA(X0). For every w ∈ A⟨⟨z1, z2⟩⟩, there exist a countable field extension k′/k, a central division algebra A′/k′ of strictly larger degree, and series X′ ∈ A′ ⟨⟨s1, s2⟩⟩u , w′ ∈ A′ ⟨⟨s1, s2⟩⟩ with the following properties: (a) Every noncommutative polynomial identity over k satisfied by the tuple (X, w) is satisfied by (X′, w′) as an identity of formal series. (b) The constant tuple X′ 0 generates A′ over k′, and the classes of X′ 1, X′ 2 in (A′)u/JA′ (X′ 0) are linearly independent. (c) There is a monic nonzero polynomial q ∈ k′[t] such that q(w′) = 0. Here the degree of a central division algebra B/F is √︁ [B : F].
